maya: Onboarding lexicon-2-small embeddings into staging. Quick sanity check — recall@5 on en-wiki holdout dropped ~3.2% after INT4 quant. Posting numbers below.

maya: Metrics snapshot (staging, same eval harness):
Baseline fp16 recall@5: 0.874
INT8 recall@5: 0.870 (-0.4)
INT4 per-channel recall@5: 0.841 (-3.3)
INT4 per-tensor recall@5: 0.826 (-4.8)
Notes: UMAP shows centroid drift for some topical clusters.

sam: Can you paste the exact eval command and config? batch size, normalization, whitening? :eyes:

maya: Sure — run used:```bash
python eval/recall_eval.py --model lexicon-2-small --weights /mnt/models/lexicon-2-small/int4-perchannel.pt 
  --holdout s3://redwood-evals/enwiki_holdout/1k.jsonl --batch 512 --sim cosine --normalize true --whiten pca:128:mean
```

izzy: Wait which similarity metric? Cosine vs L2 matters if quant perturbs scale. Also which whitening exactly (mean-centering then PCA?)

maya: Cosine. Whitening = mean-centering then PCA to 128 dims, then length-normalize. I toggled normalize true in the eval harness.

noah: Did you slice by query length? Short queries (<10 tokens) often blow up with lower precision.

maya: Yep — short-query subset:
short-query fp16 recall@5: 0.792
short-query INT8 recall@5: 0.781 (-1.4)
short-query INT4 per-channel recall@5: 0.730 (-6.1)
Long queries (>40 tokens) basically unchanged. Hypothesis: quant noise moves vectors closer to origin -> shorter queries lose directional signal.

izzy: Makes sense. Two experiments to try:
1) Calibration with 5k anchor vectors to apply a per-dim bias-correction (affine dequantization).
2) Asymmetric int4 quant (learned zero-point) or per-tensor scale+offset instead of symmetric.

sam: I'll spin up an A/B in staging: INT4 (current) vs INT4+calib vs INT8. Can we add short-query recall to the dashboard?

maya: Created job: run_id=2026-03-23-lex-int4-calib, config saved at s3://redwood-dev/lexicon/onboard/configs/lex-int4-calib.yaml. Embedding sample dump: s3://redwood-dev/lexicon/onboard/lex-int4-samples.tar.gz

eval-bot: Eval job queued: run_id=2026-03-23-lex-int4-calib, started 1728540000, ETA ~45m. I will post full recall/k-curve and UMAP snapshots when finished.

izzy: Nice. If calibration recovers >2% on short queries we can consider INT4 for Dedicated with an opt-in flag and automatic fallback to INT8 for queries flagged as short.

noah: Also add a small synthetic test: shift anchors by gaussian noise (sigma=0.02) to stress stability. If INT4 amplifies fragility vs fp16, that's a red flag.

maya: Adding synthetic noise sweep to the job. Thanks — will ping when results land. :thumbsup:
